name: California Federal Surplus Property Program
description: Access to federal surplus property through the State of California for eligible public agencies and nonprofit organizations, for a service and handling fee
fullDescription: The California Department of General Services' Federal Surplus Personal Property Program (FSPP) obtains federal surplus property for qualifying public agencies and nonprofit organizations ("donees") in California, for a service and handling fee instead of the full cost.
whatTheyOffer:
- Federal surplus personal property for your organization's operations
- Items may include furniture, office equipment, vehicles, electronics, tools, and more (availability varies)
- Service and handling fee instead of purchase price (flat $100 or a percentage of original acquisition cost, e.g. 0-30% for items under $15,000)
howToGetIt:
1. Check the federal eligibility guidelines (public agencies, schools, libraries, museums, nonprofit health providers, providers serving homeless or low-income people, programs for older adults, certain veterans and service organizations, and volunteer fire departments)
2. Submit the donee eligibility application to DGS
3. Once approved, request available federal surplus property
4. Agree to use restrictions and pay the service and handling fee
5. Pick up items directly or arrange your own pickup
keywords: federal surplus, California DGS, nonprofit equipment, vehicles, technology, medical equipment, tools, machinery, donee, 501c3, government property
